name: Northshore
tagline: Boutiques, galleries, and riverfront lawns between the bridges.
description: Located across the Tennessee River from Downtown, Chattanooga's Northshore is a vibrant neighborhood filled with independent boutiques, locally owned restaurants, coffee shops, public art, and green spaces. Its walkable streets, welcoming atmosphere, and riverfront parks make it a favorite for both visitors and locals.
special: Walk off the Walnut Street Bridge and you land on the lawn at Coolidge Park, with a carousel on one side and Frazier Avenue's shops on the other. The stretch locals call "between the bridges" packs artist-run galleries, a decades-old bookstore, ice cream, doughnuts, and patios into a few easy blocks. History runs deep here too: after Emancipation, this area was settled as Hill City, a town with a Black majority that later became part of Chattanooga.

hero.alt: Aerial view of Coolidge Park's carousel pavilion, the Walnut Street Bridge, and Frazier Avenue storefronts

walkingRoute.name: Bridges & Frazier Loop
walkingRoute.description: About 1.5 miles. Cross the Walnut Street Bridge, explore Coolidge Park, stroll east on Frazier Avenue, detour to Renaissance Park, then return over the Market Street Bridge. Route line is approximate — follow sidewalks and crosswalks.

name: Downtown
tagline: The aquarium, the bluff, and the riverfront — all within a few blocks.
description: Downtown Chattanooga brings together the city's most recognizable attractions, vibrant riverfront, historic architecture, museums, restaurants, and entertainment venues. From the Tennessee Aquarium to the Bluff View Art District, Downtown offers an excellent introduction to the Scenic City. Just west of the center, the historic Westside District and the Riverwalk past Blue Goose Hollow round out the area.
special: Chattanooga's riverfront transformation is one of the great American comeback stories, and Downtown is where you can see it best: the terraced lawns of Ross's Landing step down to the water where the city began, the Aquarium's glass peaks rise beside them, and the Hunter Museum and Bluff View Art District sit on the cliffs above. Broad Street ties it together with places to eat, play, and catch a show. Head west along the Riverwalk to Blue Goose Hollow and Westside Park in the Westside District, one of the city's oldest neighborhoods — mostly residential, so explore respectfully.

hero.alt: Aerial view of the Tennessee Aquarium and Ross's Landing on the downtown riverfront

walkingRoute.name: Riverfront & Bluff Stroll
walkingRoute.description: About 1.25 miles. Start at Ross's Landing, pass the Tennessee Aquarium, follow the riverfront east to the Walnut Street Bridge, then climb to the Hunter Museum and Bluff View Art District. Route line is approximate.

name: Southside
tagline: Main Street eats, the South Broad District, and historic St. Elmo.
description: The Southside is Chattanooga's creative and culinary playground, known for independent restaurants, coffee shops, breweries, live music, galleries, and historic industrial architecture. Centered around Main Street and the historic Chattanooga Choo Choo, this district offers some of the city's most memorable dining and nightlife experiences. Farther south along Broad Street, the South Broad District and the Victorian streets of historic St. Elmo at the foot of Lookout Mountain round out the area.
special: Old warehouses and rail lines have become bakeries, butcher counters, music halls, and art parks. Start at the Choo Choo's grand 1909 terminal, slip down Station Street for live music, grab bread at Niedlov's, and finish with sculpture and kites at Sculpture Fields. Keep going down Broad Street to catch a Lookouts game at Erlanger Park, then end the day in St. Elmo — one of Chattanooga's oldest suburbs and a National Register historic district — with a meal and a stroll past porch-lined homes.

hero.alt: The Chattanooga Choo Choo locomotive in red, green, and gold

walkingRoute.name: Main Street Food Walk
walkingRoute.description: About 1.25 miles. Start at Main Terrain Art Park, walk east along Main Street past Hi-Fi Clyde's, loop through the Choo Choo and Station Street, then continue to Niedlov's and Main Street Meats. Route line is approximate.

name: Lookout Mountain
tagline: Waterfalls, overlooks, and Civil War history high above the city.
description: Rising above Chattanooga on the Tennessee–Georgia line, Lookout Mountain is home to some of the region's best-known attractions: an underground waterfall, one of the steepest passenger railways in the world, sweeping overlooks, and the Civil War battlefield at Point Park.
special: Ride the 1895 Incline Railway up from St. Elmo, walk out to the overlooks at Point Park, a National Park Service site, then head inside the mountain to see Ruby Falls. Zip through the treetops at Ruby Falls' High Point ZIP Adventure, and finish just over the Georgia line at Rock City's gardens and Lover's Leap. Allow time — the attractions are spread across the mountain and most visitors drive between them.

hero.alt: Rock City's sandstone cliffs on Lookout Mountain overlooking the valley
